key: And it was so from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day.
s: After the rout of the Amalekite raiders, David rules that the men left behind at the brook share the spoil; Rashi, on 30:25, reads ‘forward’, in Hebrew ‘and upward’, as reaching back in time, since Abraham had already set this rule.

evidence.gloss: It does not say ‘onward’ but ‘and upward’ [that is, before]: Abraham had already set this statute (Genesis 14:24), ‘save only that which the young men have eaten’, those who sat by the baggage, ‘and the portion of the men’, those who went to war.

reason: Opened packet.js tanakh 96 --verse 30.25: Rashi on מהיום ההוא ומעלה writes לא נאמר והלאה, אלא ומעלה, כבר הנהיג אברהם בחוק זה (Genesis 14:24). The problem holds: the sentence said only ‘the Hebrew wording’ while the JPS key prints ‘forward’, so the reader could not see which word Rashi turns. Corrected as the critic proposed: the reading now names ‘forward’ (one word of the key, in curly quotes) and gives the Hebrew ומעלה as ‘and upward’, then the reach back to Abraham, all in Rashi’s own words at the place named; the context clause keeps the refuter’s fix (the men left behind at the brook) and drops ‘with those who fought’ for length.
